title: Java developer tools used in day-to-day work
answer: As a Java developer, the tools I commonly work with include IntelliJ IDEA for coding, navigation, refactoring, debugging, and Spring support; JDK tools for compiling and running Java; Maven for dependency management and build automation; Git for source control; and automated test tooling such as JUnit through the Maven build. For API development I use tools such as Postman, while database work may involve SQL clients or database IDEs depending on the platform. For delivery and operations I am familiar with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins or GitHub Actions, container tooling such as Docker, and deployment platforms such as Kubernetes when the project requires them. I also use logs, metrics, profilers, and command-line diagnostics during troubleshooting. The exact tool set depends on the project, but I prefer a reproducible workflow where the IDE, build, source control, tests, and CI all agree on the same project configuration.

steps.title: Start with IntelliJ IDEA
steps.question: IntelliJ gives the project one place for source navigation, typed refactoring, inspections, debugging, framework awareness, build integration, and terminal access. A Java developer's tool set should support the whole coding cycle rather than only text editing. Why is IntelliJ IDEA useful for navigation, refactoring, inspections, debugging, and Spring-aware development in one workspace?
steps.why: IntelliJ gives the project one place for source navigation, typed refactoring, inspections, debugging, framework awareness, build integration, and terminal access.
steps.why_te: AeroTopo project ni IntelliJ lo open chesi start cheddam. IntelliJ source navigation, safe refactoring, inspections, debugging, Spring awareness, build integration mariyu terminal access ni oka workspace lo istundi. Anduke Java development lo IDE central tool ga useful.

steps.title: Inspect the configured JDK
steps.question: The JDK controls the compiler, runtime, language level, diagnostics, and many command-line utilities, so its version directly affects what the project can build and run. The IDE is only one part of the environment; Java itself is provided by the JDK. Why should a Java developer treat the configured JDK as a core development tool rather than an invisible machine dependency?
steps.why: The JDK controls the compiler, runtime, language level, diagnostics, and many command-line utilities, so its version directly affects what the project can build and run.
steps.why_te: Project SDK ikkada kanipistundi. AeroTopo Java 21 use chestunda ani easy ga check cheyyachu. IntelliJ wrong JDK use chesthe compile errors leda wrong language features kanipinchachu.

steps.title: Use Maven for the build
steps.question: Maven makes the build portable and repeatable outside IntelliJ, which is essential for teammates and CI systems. Enterprise Java projects depend on many libraries and repeatable lifecycle tasks. Why is Maven a core tool for dependency management, compilation, testing, and packaging instead of leaving those tasks to IDE-specific buttons?
steps.why: Maven makes the build portable and repeatable outside IntelliJ, which is essential for teammates and CI systems.
steps.why_te: Maven window lo dependencies, plugins and lifecycle goals kanipistayi. Project ela build avutundo ikkada easy ga check cheyyachu. Same Maven setup local machine and CI lo use avutundi.

steps.title: Use Git for source control
steps.question: Git records change history, supports branches and diffs, and provides the basis for code review, collaboration, rollback, and CI triggers. Java development is collaborative and every production change needs traceability. What role does Git play beyond simply keeping a backup of source files?
steps.why: Git records change history, supports branches and diffs, and provides the basis for code review, collaboration, rollback, and CI triggers.
steps.why_te: Git window lo changed files and current branch kanipistayi. Code lo em marchamo commit mundu ikkada check cheyyachu. Wrong change unte diff chusi easy ga identify cheyyachu.

steps.title: Inspect Spring-aware tooling
steps.question: Framework-aware tooling helps connect source code to the runtime concepts Spring creates around it, reducing the effort needed to navigate a large application. A Spring Boot application contains framework concepts that are not obvious from individual Java files. Why is Spring-aware IDE tooling useful when working with beans, mappings, properties, and application lifecycle?
steps.why: Framework-aware tooling helps connect source code to the runtime concepts Spring creates around it, reducing the effort needed to navigate a large application.
steps.why_te: Spring view lo project beans kanipistayi. Java class Spring manage chestunna object ga runtime lo load ayinda ani ikkada check cheyyachu. Project grow ayina appudu bean ekkada undi ani find cheyyadaniki ee view useful.

steps.title: Use the integrated terminal
steps.question: Direct command execution exposes the real tools used by CI and production troubleshooting and makes environment problems easier to diagnose. A graphical IDE does not replace command-line verification. Why should Java developers remain comfortable running build, Git, runtime, and diagnostic commands from a terminal?
steps.why: Direct command execution exposes the real tools used by CI and production troubleshooting and makes environment problems easier to diagnose.
steps.why_te: IntelliJ terminal ni open chesi commands run cheddam. Terminal nundi direct commands run chesthe CI use chese real tools tho same behavior verify cheyyachu. Environment, build mariyu troubleshooting problems ni diagnose cheyyadam kuda easy avutundi.

steps.title: Check Java from the terminal
steps.question: It confirms the runtime executable that commands will use, preventing version drift from being mistaken for a source-code problem. When several JDKs are installed, IDE configuration and shell PATH can disagree. What does checking `java --version` tell you about the actual Java tool being used in the current terminal?
steps.why: It confirms the runtime executable that commands will use, preventing version drift from being mistaken for a source-code problem.
steps.why_te: Ee command run chesi output ni chudandi. `java --version` current terminal actual ga ye Java runtime use chestundo confirm chestundi. Version drift ni source-code issue laga confuse avvakunda help chestundi.

steps.title: Check Maven from the terminal
steps.question: It verifies both Maven and the Java runtime Maven is using, which helps expose local build-tool mismatches early. The Maven tool window is convenient, but the command-line build is what CI commonly executes. Why is `mvn -version` a useful toolchain check for a Java developer?
steps.why: It verifies both Maven and the Java runtime Maven is using, which helps expose local build-tool mismatches early.
steps.why_te: Ee command run chesi output ni chudandi. `mvn -version` Maven version mariyu Maven use chestunna Java runtime renditini chupistundi. Local build-tool mismatch ni mundhe identify cheyyadaniki idi useful.

steps.title: Check Git from the terminal
steps.question: It proves the underlying Git client is present independently of the IDE integration, which matters for scripts, hooks, and CI-style workflows. Source control operations may be performed through IntelliJ or from the command line. Why is checking `git --version` useful when describing a reproducible Java development tool set?
steps.why: It proves the underlying Git client is present independently of the IDE integration, which matters for scripts, hooks, and CI-style workflows.
steps.why_te: Ee command run chesi output ni chudandi. `git --version` underlying Git client IDE integration ki separate ga available undani confirm chestundi. Scripts, hooks mariyu CI-style workflows lo idi important.

steps.title: Finish with automated verification
steps.question: The test gate exercises the JDK, Maven build, dependencies, compiled code, and test framework together and therefore provides evidence that the development toolchain is coherent. A long list of tools is not valuable unless they work together consistently. Why should a Java developer prove the environment with the project's automated test command before considering the toolchain ready?
steps.why: The test gate exercises the JDK, Maven build, dependencies, compiled code, and test framework together and therefore provides evidence that the development toolchain is coherent.
steps.why_te: Maven goal run chesi build result ni chudandi. Automated test gate JDK, Maven build, dependencies, compiled code mariyu test framework anni kalisi correct ga work chestunnayi ani prove chestundi. Tool list kanna ee same result icche verification mukhyam.
